title: Cryptography and Security
description: Security as adversarial engineering: threat models, symmetric and public-key cryptography, authentication, protocols, software flaws, and risk management.
overview: Security claims are only meaningful relative to assets, principals, trust boundaries, adversary capabilities, and evidence. The course therefore moves from mathematical primitives to protocol traces and operational risk rather than treating cryptography as a catalogue of algorithms.

required: Probability, modular arithmetic, and basic networks
